problem: Sales were reportedly very low and the monthly plan was priced like a smartphone.
title: Microsoft cancels the Kin phone about six weeks after launch
context: Microsoft launched the Kin, a social-network-focused phone, on Verizon in mid-April 2010.
decision_made: Stop the Kin and focus on Windows Phone 7, and not ship the Kin in Europe as planned.
action_taken: Verizon cut prices from $49 to $29 and from $99 to $49 shortly before cancellation.
observed_outcome: The phone was pulled after about 48 days. Sales estimates range from about 500 to under 10,000 units; Microsoft never confirmed a figure.
lessons: A product positioned between categories, with pricing that matched a different one, can fail very quickly.
limitations: The 500-unit figure is a rumour, and the 48-day figure is repeated across sources but described variously as six weeks or two months.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft said it would focus on Windows Phone 7 and not ship the Kin in Europe as planned.
Microsoft pulled the Kin just over two months after its debut.
